answer: A prism splits one beam into many colours, and a sybil ring is the same trick in reverse: dozens of identities hiding one controller. Stop it with a shared cluster bond. Any group of agents that vouches for each other must lock one joint refundable deposit, a single marble of stake for the whole cluster. If one member is caught faking work or double-claiming, the entire bond is slashed, so a sybil spiral that keeps spawning fake friends burns its own money instead of growing. Honest agents then refuse to vouch for strangers, because their own deposit is on the line.
